evidence.quote: there\u2019s a bit of rope round the dead man\u2019s leg. Don\u2019t you see that other bit of rope up there caught at the corner of the window?
evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown reasons from physical clues (matching rope fragments) to deduce the body fell from the window.

evidence.quote: At the beginning you said we\u2019d found no weapon. But now we\u2019re finding too many; there\u2019s the knife to stab, and the rope to strangle, and the pistol to shoot; and after all he broke his neck by falling out of a window! It won\u2019t do. It\u2019s not economical.
evidence.paraphrase: The priest applies logical scrutiny to the improbable abundance of weapons, treating it as a problem to be solved.

evidence.quote: First, these holes in the carpet, where the six bullets have gone in. Why on earth should anybody fire at the carpet?
evidence.paraphrase: Brown reasons through the physical evidence, noting the bullet holes in the carpet are inconsistent with an attack on a person.

evidence.quote: you noticed that he left blood, but no wound, on that servant\u2019s face?
evidence.paraphrase: Brown draws attention to observed details\u2014blood without a wound\u2014to reconstruct the events.

evidence.quote: there is this horror about alcoholism in a sincere teetotaler: that he pictures and expects that psychological inferno from which he has warned others
evidence.paraphrase: A psychological explanation is offered for how the victim's abstinence-based expectations led to his suicidal breakdown.

evidence.quote: Merton felt an almost bodily sickness at the sight of him
evidence.paraphrase: Merton reacts with visceral disgust to the servant Magnus.

evidence.quote: The girl uttered a startled, singular little cry; everyone looked at her. Her figure was rigid as if paralysed
evidence.paraphrase: Alice reacts with shock and paralysis when the accusation is raised.

evidence.quote: I\u2019m not sure that the Armstrong cheerfulness is so very cheerful\u2014for other people.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrative contrasts the public image of cheerfulness with a darker reality experienced by those around Armstrong.
